title: Economy edges back into expansion in October, PMI shows
excerpt: The index rose to 51.8 after two months of contraction, led by farming. New orders still shrank in industry, construction and services.

image.alt: Goods stacked outside shops at Karwan Bazar, Dhaka's main wholesale market
image.credit: mohigan / Panoramio via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

content:
Bangladesh’s Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose 3.2 points to 51.8 in October, returning to expansion after two months of contraction, The Business Standard reported. A reading above 50 means activity is growing. The index is published by the Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MCCI), Dhaka, and Policy Exchange Bangladesh.

Behind the numbers

  • Agriculture has expanded for 14 months in a row.
  • In manufacturing, employment and stocks grew, but new orders, export orders and output still fell, and input prices rose sharply.
  • Construction and services also added jobs while new business shrank. Input costs stayed high across all sectors.

M Masrur Reaz, chairman and chief executive of Policy Exchange Bangladesh, called it a “small but positive development” but said the recovery “remained fragile” because demand had not yet strengthened across the economy.

Why it matters

The October reading came during weeks of garment wage protests and factory closures, which may weigh on the November figure. With the World Bank estimating that poverty rose again in FY26 and input prices still climbing, a modest pick-up in activity is unlikely to ease pressure on poor households quickly. Rising employment in the index is worth watching for livelihood programmes.

Limitations

The PMI is a survey of purchasing managers’ views, not official output data. One month above 50 does not make a trend.

Sources

  • Bangladesh economy returns to expansion after two months of contraction: PMI, The Business Standard, 10 November 2026
